column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout, its dates; record checked: the tab l.10 (lock 1 Oct), l.11 (objection 5 Oct), l.14 (fills 7-8 Oct, Sydney per NUMBERS 8b) hold; one clause at most, say before money moved, never at the midpoint; MBA project teams, so context not proof.
Wed 18 Nov: same paper and same use as row 1 (date the objection); a methodological detail, store only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f guard with a reason; record checked: no feelings, replies or tone (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM l.63-65, l.121), so 3f calls the argument neither friendly nor heated; restates an existing guard, store only.

Wed 18 Nov: record checked: the journal l.23 (Caplet's doc, writer unnamed) and the tab l.11 name Darren, so 3f simply names him; it claims no safety and never we recorded it as evidence of a climate; team size second-hand; near H9-177.
Wed 18 Nov: the 23% is the BPS Digest's; check it in De Dreu and Weingart before any use; background to Q91-009 only.
Wed 18 Nov: top teams, abstract only; its use restates SKELETON 3f's ending (VT kept for Laura's reasons); store only.
Wed 18 Nov: same use as row 11 (claim no unanimity), which is read at source with quotes; Amason's correlations unread.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q91-013 (an absence of dissent should sound an alarm), already planned for 3f's closing; record checked: Darren's is the one recorded argument between teammates (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM section 4); HBR practitioner piece.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout: the 30 Sep bar may be told as what happened (a test fixed before the trade found ..., 30 Sep model, dated), never we ran; but the record never says the 5 Oct choice turned on it (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM l.122), so say the bar already existed, never that the number settled the argument.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout; record checked: the tab l.11 holds picking stocks and ETFs, EWT and GLD raised and VT kept, so a choice among four stands; say raised, never weighed or tested (the 30 Sep test's four were other funds, gold the only overlap); who raised EWT and GLD stays unsaid.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout; record checked: the tab l.11's We decided, in the end (Caplet's own edit) claims no vote and no unanimity, and no reply from Darren is in the record (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM l.121), so never we all agreed or Darren came round; a reason for an existing guard.

Wed 18 Nov: by Lind's own design 5 Oct is voice after the decision (the 1 Oct lock in the tab l.10), not before it; say only that it came while a change could still alter what was bought (fills 7-8 Oct Sydney); fairness, not decision quality.
Wed 18 Nov: its 3f use (Darren's case at full strength) is row 27's; the commitment and trust it measures are outcomes the record does not show; abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: IPS l.17 checked; the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy: a fixed rule can itself entrap, and the two reasons are exits for when the plan cannot be carried out, not a test of failure; no unanimity rule in the record; at most 3c or 3e, never 3f.
Wed 18 Nov: record checked: no vote (PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM l.121); its use (tell 5 Oct as options raised) is row 10's; hidden-profile lab tasks, abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout, a candidate for the one clause of evidence beside Q91-030 and Q91-021; one recorded objection is not a norm, so never claim the team had a norm of criticism; use only as why a real objection is worth having; undergraduates, hiring task.
Wed 18 Nov: same paper's pilot (8 groups of four); row 16 carries the result.
Wed 18 Nov: 3f guard: no Caplet record uses groupthink, so the word stays out; this row gives the reason (Turner and Pratkanis read in full); store only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout, what we understand now (SO 21) about the alternative Darren proposed (the tab l.11; the journal l.23, normal stock and ETF picking): groups of amateurs picking trailed the index; fits RANKING_4 reason 3 or 4 better than households alone; never as said on 5 Oct or aimed at Darren; one clause; US clubs 1991-97.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout aha, usable with fixes: the paper shows groups drawn to admired picks, not to index funds, so say the objection names a real risk (choosing the easy reason) without claiming research shows groups favour VT; the 30 Sep test covered gold, not picking or EWT, so it answers gold only; 0.8991 met the ratio and failed the every-run clause, never within a thousandth of passing; told as what happened, never as the 5 Oct answer.

Wed 18 Nov: same paper and mechanism as row 20; its caution (TN3 at most once, never the moral) is SKELETON 3f's already; never call the team's own reason rhetorically safe in the report; Irwin and Davis only as quoted.

Wed 18 Nov: breaks on its own figure: Harrington counts school ties with work ties as the 8% better case, so classmates are not the friends-and-family case; nothing on Caplet's friendships is in the record; a press release, the article not reached.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout, a writer's guard; record checked: the tab l.11 and the journal l.23 carry the word copout with the proposal (picking stocks and ETFs), so 3f keeps both in one sentence; never the terms exploratory or disputational in the report; primary-school research.
Wed 18 Nov: same research programme as row 23; serves no part.
Wed 18 Nov: provable puzzles; row 26 states the limit that matters (a fund choice has no provable answer, so a bar written first makes only part of it checkable); Q91-016 holds the argument theory.

Wed 18 Nov: the bar of 30 Sep made the gold question checkable (told as what happened, never we ran); picking and EWT were not in that test and stay judgments answered by Laura's reasons; never that the 5 Oct decision rested on it or that a majority was avoided (no vote in the record); a writer's guide, not report text.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout craft rule, read at source and stronger than H5-014's second-hand figures (r .077 against -.049); Darren's case only in the record's words (copout; picking stocks and ETFs); answered by the bar already written (told as what happened) and Laura's reasons, TN3 at most once; never as the reply given on 5 Oct; small effects.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout; its details all stand (5 Oct, Darren as the record names him, EWT and GLD, the 30 Sep test dated as that day's model, TNA l.23); pair with row 29, since a judge can check the TNA and IPS but not the 30 Sep figure; built for suspect interviews.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f, the refinement that makes row 28 usable: under an incentive to look credible only details a judge can check count, so lean on TNA l.23 and the IPS the judges hold, with the 30 Sep figure dated and kept to one; abstract and replication read.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f guard against a conversion story (never we were wrong to doubt or Darren taught us humility; the record holds neither, PEOPLE_IN_THE_ROOM l.121); the 2009 article read only as quoted in the Huddersfield paper, so cite it as secondary; beside Q80-023.
Wed 18 Nov: same use as Q80-007 (assessors cannot verify reflections, so point each claim at a dated record); the 20% is second-hand.

Wed 18 Nov: 3f copout, the costly admission is the close call, said correctly: gold with property met the ratio on average (0.8991 against 0.90) but passed on only about four runs in five, so failed the every-run clause (30 Sep model, dated, told as what happened); a second one in the record: the first written reason came 18 days later (TNA l.23); the hearsay rule guides writers only, never in the report or References.

Wed 18 Nov: record checked: the tab l.11 (We decided, in the end) and Wharton's influenced (instructions l.129-130) hold, so never changed our decision; VT kept with a test fixed first may stand, told as what happened; keep the 30 Sep test's four funds (tested) apart from the 5 Oct options (raised), never four alternatives weighed for both.

Wed 18 Nov: four dates are Caplet's record (the tab l.10, l.11, l.14; TNA l.23); the 30 Sep test is in the decision file (D_fund_choice.md l.4), not the team's tab or journal, so drop from the team's own record but keep the date, told as what happened; test before reason holds; fills 7-8 Oct Sydney; row 12 does not make 5 Oct voice before a decision.
